elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Rendered 14.2: "Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable and work product created for Customer" — direction of ownership is reversed from Vendor to Customer and expressly covers work product as well as the defined Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: Rendered 14.2: "Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable and work product" — present-tense operative assignment, not an agreement to assign.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.3: "Vendor retains Vendor Technology"; clause 1.8 defines Vendor Technology as Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines and connectors. Unchanged by the redline.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Retained 13.2 grants a "perpetual ... licence" for Vendor Technology "embedded in a Deliverable", and 14.3 expressly channels incorporated Vendor Technology into "the perpetual licence in Section 13.2". Cross-reference survives intact.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Retained 13.2: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence".

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Retained 13.2: "royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from" for Customer's business.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.1 first sentence: "Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services", and "No right transfers to Vendor except" the narrowed processing right.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Rendered 14.1: "the limited right to process that material solely to provide the Services for Customer" (the "secure, support, and improve" uses are gone), and rendered 15.1: "Vendor shall process Customer Data solely to provide the Services and on Customer's documented instructions" with the consent-based sale/advertising/model-training exception deleted, so no consent-gated or "permitted by this Agreement" residual use survives.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.4: "No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights" — any future joint ownership requires a separate signed instrument specifying exploitation rights.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: 14.3 preserves Vendor Technology ownership, and definitions 1.4/1.8 exclude from Deliverables "generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Condition for a licence does not arise as to Deliverables themselves: rendered 14.2 vests exclusive ownership plus assignment in Customer, which subsumes a perpetual licence; embedded Vendor Technology is separately licensed perpetually under 13.2.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Customer owns the Deliverables outright under 14.2 (assignment of all right, title and interest), so there is no revocable licence; the prior "revocable, non-transferable licence" wording is deleted. Embedded Vendor IP is irrevocably licensed under 13.2.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Ownership under 14.2 carries no territorial limit; 13.2's licence to embedded Vendor Technology is expressly "worldwide".

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No further payment is attached to Customer's ownership in 14.2; 13.2 is "royalty-free, fully paid" for embedded Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: As exclusive owner and assignee under 14.2, Customer may use and modify without restriction; 13.2 separately permits "modify, create derivative works from" embedded Vendor Technology, and 14.3 bars third-party material that materially restricts Customer's intended use.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Ownership under 14.2 includes the right to sublicense; the former "non-transferable" restriction in 14.2 is removed.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Same as preferred: rendered 14.1 ("solely to provide the Services for Customer") and rendered 15.1 ("solely to provide the Services and on Customer's documented instructions"), with "improve the Services", "as permitted by this Agreement" and the consent carve-out all removed.

reasons: Classification is correct: original 14.2 gave Vendor exclusive ownership of Deliverables Customer paid for and left Customer only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence — a fallback failure and walk-away-adjacent, so a redline is warranted rather than a rationale note.

All nine preferred elements are met in operative language: 14.2 flips ownership and adds a present-tense assignment covering both Deliverables and work product; 14.3 and 13.2 (unchanged) preserve Vendor Technology and the perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free embedded-IP licence with the 13.2 cross-reference intact; 14.1 preserves Customer Data ownership; 14.4 preserves the no-joint-ownership default.

The Customer Data element is fully closed in both places it appeared: 14.1's "secure, support, and improve" uses and 15.1's "as permitted by this Agreement" plus the consent-gated sale/advertising/model-training carve-out are removed, so no residual broad or consent-based Vendor exploitation right defeats "solely to provide the Services". Narrowing both provisions was necessary to avoid an internally inconsistent retained sentence, not duplication.

Minimality holds: edits are confined to 14.2 (ownership/assignment) and the two Customer Data use provisions; the deletion of the old revocable licence sentence is consequential on Customer ownership, and no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra requirement outside the checklist was added. Deleting "without Customer's express written consent" in 15.1 is required by the checklist element (consent-based use defeats "solely to provide") and also strengthens Customer's position.

Intent is preserved: 14.3's reference to "the perpetual licence in Section 13.2" and the Vendor Technology identification/third-party approval duties survive, the feedback mechanic in 14.4 is untouched, 15.1 retains the documented-instructions control, and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created.

No repair needed. Optional (do not treat as a defect): if Order Forms elsewhere assume Vendor ownership of Deliverables, confirm no conflicting Order Form or exhibit language survives against new 14.2.
